name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
rangeNote: The Institute of Medicine considers 50 nmol/L (20 ng/mL) enough for bone health in most people; levels above 125 nmol/L (50 ng/mL) may carry risks.
summary: This test measures 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the storage form of vitamin D. Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium and keep bones strong.

high.meaning: A high level almost always comes from taking a lot of vitamin D supplements. Very high levels can raise calcium in the blood.

low.meaning: A low level means vitamin D stores are low, which over time can weaken bones.
commonCauses: Little sun exposure, especially in winter

sources.title: The 2011 report on dietary reference intakes for calcium and vitamin D from the Institute of Medicine: what clinicians need to know
